formula: Sales ~ Promo + SchoolHoliday + StateHoliday + CompetitionDistance + CompetitionOpenSinceMonth + CompetitionOpenSinceYear + Promo2 + Promo2SinceWeek + Promo2SinceYear + PromoInterval + StoreType + Assortment + (1 | Store)
notes: Read: Simchoni and Rosset (LMMNN, arXiv 2206.03314) Sec. 5.2.2 and Table 8 (Rossmann: 1.1K stores, 25-31 monthly measures, "Total $ sales (in 100K)", "random terms in t up to a quadratic with no correlations between these terms"); Sigrist 2023 Table 1 and run_experiments.R ((1 |Store) + (0 + t|Store) + (0 + I(t^2)|Store), gpboost with uncorrelated slopes); LMMNN's lme4 baseline (r_scripts/lme4_on_datasets/lme4_rossmann.R) writes (1 + t + I(t^2)|Store), correlated. Preprocessing (rossmann_etl.R in both repositories): daily sales summed per store and month and divided by 1e5, Open, Promo, SchoolHoliday and the StateHoliday dummies summed per month, store data imputed by medians (PromoInterval NA as a level), t = days since 2013-01-01 over its maximum; on this daily table the terms are the same columns per day. BeyondArena keeps open days only and drops Open and Customers; its task has no group_on. DayOfWeek is not a documented term. Hand check #162: the published model fits monthly aggregates with time slopes per store, so on this daily table the model is the reader's proposal, without the time terms and slopes.

formula: log(Income) ~ log(TotalPop) + I(Men/TotalPop) + I(Women/TotalPop) + Hispanic + White + Black + Native + Asian + Pacific + I(VotingAgeCitizen/TotalPop) + Poverty + ChildPoverty + Professional + Service + Office + Construction + Production + Drive + Carpool + Transit + Walk + OtherTransp + WorkAtHome + MeanCommute + I(Employed/TotalPop) + PrivateWork + PublicWork + SelfEmployed + FamilyWork + Unemployment + one county effect per State:County, a Gaussian process with an RBF kernel over the county centroids (lat, long, joined from a county file, not in the table)
notes: RULE GAP: a Gaussian-process spatial random effect has no lme4 form; the county indexes it, so State:County groups (County names repeat across states). Read: Simchoni and Rosset (LMMNN, arXiv 2206.03314) Sec. 5.2.3, Table 10 (Income: 71K tracts, 1-2K per location, p = 30, "3K US counties", "Ann. income $ (log)") and Appendix 4 Table 31; r_scripts/ETL/us_income_etl.R and notebooks/spatial/us_income.ipynb (mode spatial, q_spatial = the counties, two spatial variance parameters, no grouped random effect). Preprocessing: joins county centroids by CountyId, divides Men, Women, Employed and VotingAgeCitizen by TotalPop, logs TotalPop, rescales the percentages, keeps counties within latitude 20-50 and longitude -150 to -50, drops rows with any missing value; the network also takes the centroid coordinates as inputs. IncomeErr, IncomePerCap and IncomePerCapErr are dropped by the source. Hand check #162: the documented model is a county RBF Gaussian process beside a nonlinear fixed function, not independent county intercepts; the formula states it in words.

notes: Read: Simchoni and Rosset (LMMNN, arXiv 2206.03314) Sec. 5.2.3 and Table 10 (Cars: 97K cars, 12K US locations, categorical model (15K), "Price $ (log)"), notebooks/spatial/cars_spatial_and_categorical.ipynb (mode spatial_and_categoricals: one grouped variance on model_id, two spatial parameters on location_id) and r_scripts/ETL/cars_etl.R: distinct VIN, price 1000-300000, lat 20-50, long -150 to -50, rows without price, year, lat or long dropped, manufacturer cut to the top 10 plus other, NA as a level of every categorical, lat and long rounded to 3 decimals for the location. region and state are not documented terms. Hand check #162: the location is lat and long rounded to three decimals, a unit no column holds, so model alone groups; the network takes lat and long as inputs, so they are covariates. The longitude GLMM is model 2.

notes: Simchoni and Rosset (LMMNN, arXiv 2206.03314) Sec. 6, r_scripts/lme4_on_datasets/lme4_cars_glmm.R: glmer of long >= -1.2 on the covariates and price with a random intercept per car model (model_id), binomial, after r_scripts/ETL/cars_etl.R (distinct VIN, price 1000-300000, lat 20-50, long -150 to -50, rows without price, year, lat or long dropped, long rounded to three decimals and rescaled to [-10, 10], manufacturer cut to the top 10 plus other, NA as a level of every categorical, price and year scaled). formula: nWBV ~ `MR Delay` + Age + `M/F` + Group + `MR Delay`:Group + (1 + `MR Delay` | `Subject ID`)
notes: OASIS-2 longitudinal (Marcus et al. 2010, J Cogn Neurosci 22:2677; Mendeley tsy6rbc5d4): 150 subjects aged 60 to 96, each scanned on two or more visits at least a year apart, 373 sessions; Group is nondemented, demented or converted. BeyondArena's dementia_prediction (Table B.1: grouped multiclass) predicts Group grouped by subject, but Group is fixed per subject, so it carries no random effect. The paper follows nWBV, normalized whole-brain volume, across visits: per-subject atrophy slopes compared by age, sex and dementia status with analysis of covariance (section Estimated Total Intracranial Volume and Normalized Whole-brain Volume, Fig. 3). Rendered as a random intercept and MR Delay slope per subject with the slope differing by Group; no mixed model published. MRI ID, Visit, Hand (all right-handed), CDR and MMSE (the ratings Group is built from), eTIV and ASF (the normalization behind nWBV) are ignored; EDUC and SES stay usable. Hand check #162: the paper computes each subject's annualized atrophy rate and compares the rates by ANCOVA, the two-stage form of this slope model; Group is constant within every subject.
